text:
inc-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate against hosted endpoints in apac-region starting 2026-11-03T14:46:29Z. Paging oncall.

maria-oncall: on it. joining channel now. what are the visible symptoms?

jon-sre: seeing sustained 502/504s from the ingress LB toward inference pool in apac-east, also token errors for low-priority routes. latency up ~3x for some requests.

leah-sre: confirmed. Graphs: CPU on gpuz-1 node group spiked and we have multiple model fallback triggers. Not full OOM but queuing is high.

maria-oncall: first mitigation idea: reduce free-tier RPS and steer non-critical traffic away from apac until we scale. can we apply temporary smart-route policy?

sam-devex: yes. we have a policy template for temporary-tiering. Suggest: free -> 20 RPS, standard -> 50 RPS, enterprise stays unlimited on dedicated pools. Also add regional steer: apac low-priority -> eu-west as fallback. would add ~20-40ms to p99 but reduces load.

jon-sre: sounds good. any customers pinned to apac only? alex-support, any active enterprise customers in apac right now?

alex-support: checking. Two big enterprise customers have dedicated capacity and are pinned — not affected. A few mid-market customers have region pinned to apac but are on paid standard tier. I'll flag them if we need to steer.

maria-oncall: ok implement in this order: 1) deploy smart-route policy with tiered rate limits 2) add steering rule for low-priority apac -> eu-west fallback 3) disable non-essential features that are heavy (agg-embeddings route and optimize-cache for free tier)

ops-bot: command log: /policy apply --name temp_apac_relief --rules 'tiering,regional-steer,disable-agg'

maria-oncall: executing. putting command here for audit:

```
# apply temporary routing policy
POST /internal/v1/policies
{
  "name": "temp_apac_relief_1823456789",
  "rules": [
    {"match": {"tier": "free"}, "rate_limit_rps": 20},
    {"match": {"tier": "standard"}, "rate_limit_rps": 50},
    {"match": {"priority": "low", "region": "apac"}, "route_to": "eu-west-fallback"},
    {"match": {"route": "agg-embeddings", "tier": "free"}, "action": "disable"}
  ],
  "ttl": "30m",
  "rollout": "immediate"
}
```

ops-bot: policy apply accepted. policy_id=pol_0a9f_temp_apac_relief

leah-sre: I'm watching the routing table updates. Starting to see connections drop off apac low-priority pool.

jon-sre: ingress errors dropping at 14:49:10Z. 5xx rate down 60% in apac. queue lengths decreasing.

maria-oncall: good. can we confirm no enterprise SLA customers were routed to eu-west? wanted to keep them on dedicated pools.

raj-mlops: checked model routing rules. enterprise tenants have explicit route pins, they were excluded from the steering rule. safe.

alex-support: notifying affected standard customers about transient routing to eu-west and potential latency increase. message draft:

"Heads up — we're performing emergency traffic shaping in APAC to reduce errors. Your requests may be routed to EU-WEST temporarily; small latency increase expected (~20-50ms). No data loss."

maria-oncall: send. also open support ticket for any customers reporting errors.

sam-devex: quick note: disabling agg-embeddings on free tier may cause some SDK fallbacks; logs show a bunch of 429s from our aggregator. we'll monitor for regressions.

maria-oncall: rolling change: after 10m if metrics remain stable, we'll relax standard tier back to 80 RPS and remove the disable for agg-embeddings for standard tiers. keep free tier reduced for the duration.

jon-sre: setting alert thresholds: if apac 5xx returns to baseline and p95 latency < 2x normal for 8m, I'll trigger rampdown. else we extend TTL and consider node autoscale.

ops-bot: autoscale suggestion: add 2 nodes to gpuz-1 pool in apac-east; estimated warm-up 4-6m. approve? (yes/no)

leah-sre: approve autoscale +2. I'll queue it.

maria-oncall: do it. monitor cost impact; prioritize stability.

ops-bot: autoscale job queued. job_id=asg_021_add2

jon-sre: note — we should also temporarily raise quota for enterprise-pinned flows routed through dedicated pools if we see backpressure. leaving a TODO.

maria-oncall: good call. raj, can you create a small rollback playbook for the policy? in case eu-west saturates.

raj-mlops: creating now. will post steps and checks.

(8 minutes later)

jon-sre: apac 5xx at 14:58:30Z is back to baseline. p95 down to 1.3x. queue lengths stable. autoscale warm-up finished.

maria-oncall: nice. begin controlled rollback: increase standard RPS to 80, keep free at 20 for another 10m.

ops-bot: policy patch applied: standard.rate_limit_rps = 80

leah-sre: agg-embeddings re-enabled for standard tiers. free remains disabled.

alex-support: support message sent to affected customers. no incoming escalations yet.

maria-oncall: leaving temporary policy for 20 more minutes, then full cleanup. please add postmortem notes and assign follow-ups: - verify scaling thresholds and autoscale triggers - review routing policy test coverage - evaluate hotspot on gpuz-1 nodes

jon-sre: assigning to leah and raj for follow-ups.

leah-sre: got it.

maria-oncall: incident resolved for now. closing paging. final note: this mitigation worked; consider automating a circuit-breaker that temporarily applies this tiering policy when apac 5xx > 10/min for 5m. filing RFC.

inc-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: 1823456789 - Temporary smart-routing tiering applied, mitigated APAC 5xx spike. Duration: ~12m. Postmortem required.

maria-oncall: thanks everyone :heart: will kick off postmortem doc and schedule follow-up review.
